title: Group Classes vs Weights — Which Gym Type Is Right for You in NZ?
meta_desc: Gym classes vs weights in NZ: compare prices and contract terms
intro: When choosing a gym in New Zealand, it ultimately comes down to your personality, goals, and budget. If you're a social butterfly, group classes might be the way to go, but if you prefer solo workouts, a weights-focused gym could be more suitable. With prices ranging from $15 to $50 per week, it's essential to weigh up the costs and benefits.

sections.heading: Personality Types and Gym Preferences
sections.body: If you're an outgoing person who thrives in social environments, group classes like those offered at Les Mills (with over 40 locations across NZ) might be the perfect fit. On the other hand, if you're more introverted or prefer working out alone, a gym like Jetts (with 24/7 access and no lock-in contracts) could be more suitable.

sections.heading: ClassPass: A Hybrid Solution
sections.body: If you're torn between group classes and weights, ClassPass could be the answer. With prices starting from $49 per month for 3 classes, you can try out different gyms and classes without committing to a long-term contract. ClassPass partners with over 100 gyms in NZ, including popular chains like F45 and Orangetheory.

sections.heading: Social Factor and Motivation
sections.body: Exercising with others can be a great motivator, and group classes often provide a sense of community and accountability. However, if you prefer working out alone, you can still stay motivated by tracking your progress and setting goals. Consider what drives you and what type of environment will help you stick to your fitness routine.

sections.heading: Compare Gyms and Find the Best Deal
Les Mills Gym Review
sections.body: Les Mills is one of the most popular gym chains in NZ, with a wide range of group classes and equipment. Prices start from $24.95 per week, and you can sign up for a 12-month contract. If you're interested in learning more, check out our in-depth review.

sections.heading: Conclusion
sections.body: Ultimately, the right gym type for you will depend on your unique preferences, goals, and budget. By considering the social factor, cost per session, and contract terms, you can make an informed decision and find a gym that helps you achieve your fitness goals.
